summary: Blockchain is a decentralized, immutable distributed database or ledger shared across a network of nodes, best known for underpinning cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin but applicable to many industries. It stores data in cryptographically linked blocks, reducing reliance on trusted third parties and enabling transparent, tamper-resistant record-keeping. Common uses include financial transactions, supply chain tracking, healthcare records, property registration, and voting.

claims.text: A blockchain is a distributed database or ledger shared across a computer network's nodes.
claims.evidence_quote: A blockchain is a distributed database or ledger shared across a computer network's nodes.

claims.text: The Bitcoin blockchain stores transaction information in 4MB files called blocks.
claims.evidence_quote: The Bitcoin blockchain collects transaction information and enters it into a 4MB file called a block (different blockchains have different-sized blocks).

claims.text: Bitcoin transaction confirmation takes about one hour, based on an average block time of just under 10 minutes.
claims.evidence_quote: Confirmation takes about one hour to complete because it averages just under 10 minutes per block (the first block with your transaction and five following blocks multiplied by 10 equals 60 minutes).

claims.text: As of May 12, 2026, the Bitcoin network was hashing at a rate of around 850 exahashes per second.
claims.evidence_quote: the Bitcoin network hashed at a rate of around 850 exahashes per second as of May 12, 2026.

claims.text: As of May 12, 2026, approximately 39.06 million ETH were staked by more than one million validators on the Ethereum network.
claims.evidence_quote: As of May 12, 2026, approximately 39.06 million ETH were staked by more than one million validators.

claims.text: Blockchain technology was first outlined in 1991 by Stuart Haber and W. Scott Stornetta to timestamp documents without tampering.
claims.evidence_quote: Blockchain technology was first outlined in 1991 by Stuart Haber and W. Scott Stornetta, two researchers who wanted to implement a system where document timestamps couldn't be tampered with.

claims.text: Bitcoin is pseudonymous, not fully anonymous, because wallet addresses are viewable and can be linked to users.
claims.evidence_quote: It is a common misconception that blockchain networks like Bitcoin are fully anonymous; they are actually pseudonymous because there is a viewable address that can be associated with a user if the information gets out.

claims.text: The energy consumed by the Bitcoin network's proof-of-work system exceeds the energy usage of Finland.
claims.evidence_quote: In the real world, the energy consumed by the millions of devices on the Bitcoin network is more than what Finland uses.

claims.text: Blockchain reduces the need for trusted third parties such as auditors, who add costs and can make mistakes.
claims.evidence_quote: This reduces the need for trusted third parties, such as auditors or other humans, who add costs and can make mistakes.

claims.text: A 51% attack on the Bitcoin or other large blockchains is nearly impossible because it would require controlling at least half of the network's computational power.
claims.evidence_quote: On the Bitcoin and other larger blockchains, this is nearly impossible.

claims.text: IBM's Food Trust blockchain traces the journey of food products through the supply chain to improve transparency.
claims.evidence_quote: IBM's Food Trust blockchain can trace the journey of food products through the supply chain, showing their point of origin and the path between suppliers.

claims.text: Blockchain voting was tested in the November 2018 midterm elections in West Virginia.
claims.evidence_quote: Voting with blockchain carries the potential to eliminate election fraud and boost voter turnout, as was tested in the November 2018 midterm elections in West Virginia.

claims.text: As of 2024, The World Bank estimated that 1.3 billion adults do not have bank accounts or any means of storing money.
claims.evidence_quote: According to The World Bank, as of 2024 data, an estimated 1.3 billion adults don't have bank accounts or any means of storing their money or wealth.

claims.text: As of 2026, 47% of Americans say they will never purchase a cryptocurrency.
claims.evidence_quote: As of 2026, 47% of Americans still say they will never purchase a cryptocurrency.

claims.text: On some blockchains, transactions can be completed and considered secure in minutes.
claims.evidence_quote: On some blockchains, transactions can be completed and considered secure in minutes.
